newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Fifteen killed in Colombian political bloodshed.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen killed in Colombian political bloodshed.

text.p: At least 15 people were killed in political bloodshed across Colombia, including eight who were shot dead by right-wing gunmen in a coal-mining district of northwest Antioquia province, authorities said on Saturday.
The toll, from Friday night to Saturday morning, brought the number of Colombians killed in political-related violence since Thursday to at least 45.

The latest victims included two policemen who were killed shortly before dawn when leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels stormed a highway toll booth outside the city of Villavicencio, about 40 miles (65 km) southeast of Bogota, and reduced it to rubble with dynamite.

Police and military officials said the worst attack occurred late Friday in the municipality of Vegachi, where a group of about 20 hooded gunmen killed eight men aged between 18 and 35 and abducted at least five others who they carried off in the back of a truck.

Army and police spokesmen in Medellin, the provincial capital of Antioquia, attributed the massacre to a right-wing death squad hunting down suspected rebel sympathisers in the area but declined further comment.
In the nearby town of Yali, at least two people were killed and two policemen wounded in an attack on Friday by leftist National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas, army spokesmen said.

In the northern oil prodcution centre of Barrancabermeja, meanwhile, national radio reports said three suspected ELN rebels were killed by security force members in an aborted attempt to dynamite an oil pipeline.

Authorities said the FARC and ELN, both founded in the mid- 1960s and Latin America's largest and longest-lasting insurgency, have a combined force of about 12,000 guerrillas who operate throughout Colombia.
